identification: Urelas/MSMP configuration and network payload loader
method: Initial atomscan and cleave facts; independent Rizin and Capstone control-flow and argument tracing; PE/resource parsing, ZipCrypto extraction, exact-source YARA/YARA-X checks, and byte-level regression controls. No PE was executed and no configured sample endpoint was contacted.
evidence: PE32 entry 0x4175da reaches CRT startup and WinMain 0x4010a0. This is a readable unpacked image with residual PECompact markers and an active import directory pointing to damaged bootstrap data; original named/ordinal import descriptors survive around raw 0x358d0. Strings and family rules did not establish the verdict.

State reader 0x406d20 reads a 512-byte block via 0x406c30 or 0x406b10, complements each byte at 0x406d85, then checks MSMP at 0x406d97. Writer 0x406dd0 validates MSMP, copies and complements the same size block at 0x406e25, then stores it through 0x406a10. The writer constructs a temporary golfinfo.ini path. This is an actual transform and state roundtrip, not an entropy inference.

WinMain calls the endpoint/update loop 0x402b80. Helper 0x405d20 initializes Winsock, creates a socket, resolves addresses and connects at 0x405ed1. WS2_32 original lookup ownership and IAT sites establish ordinal 23 socket, 4 connect, 16 recv and 19 send despite missing active imports. Requests 0xBB9 and 0xBBA obtain a file manifest and file contents through 0x4065a0 and 0x4067a0. The receive result reaches a wb destination and file-transfer writer 0x4064d0 at 0x4069be. Main checks and launches that constructed Temp7%X.exe path at 0x40122b. This links remote acquisition to execution.

Installation branch 0x4015f0 derives a generated path, writes the installed image through 0x401520, and opens HKCU/Software/Microsoft/Windows NT/CurrentVersion/Windows at 0x402055. RegSetValueExW at 0x40208e writes that image path as REG_SZ to Run. The Run pointer resolves to VA 0x432f0c. The open output and write reload both use stack slot 0x18; preserved ADVAPI32 lookup entries bind the two indirect call operands to their actual API names. It then ShellExecutes the installed path at 0x4020b8.

Cleanup 0x403360 queries GetModuleFileNameA at 0x4033b2 into the buffer based at initial ESP+0x108. The formatter at 0x403480 pushes the same buffer twice for DEL and IF EXIST. Register saves and outstanding arguments account for the 32-byte displacement change. It writes a retry-delete batch through WriteFile at 0x4034b3 and launches it hidden with ShellExecuteA at 0x4034d2. The batch filename is not a required detection leg.

The raw-device path reaches a PhysicalDrive open at 0x40411f. It constructs SCSI WRITE(10) opcode 0x2A at 0x4041cf, copies a 512-byte caller buffer, and issues IOCTL_SCSI_PASS_THROUGH 0x4D004 at 0x404236. A caller constructs _GBP records. This establishes disk-write capability, not indiscriminate destruction, a successful boot infection or a disk wipe.

An encrypted ZIP is a real resource (IDR_BINARY/135), RVA/raw 0x3f0d0, size 174021, even though it is mapped in .text. ZipCrypto password 1234 recovers HanAgent_pe.exe, 195072 bytes, SHA-256 9e1d5297702d9824b192f24c2d6b32866ad2219e9ff910514d6c031ff5f82fe1. Its entry 0x41208a installs an exception handler and deliberately faults; handler 0x499094 patches a jump into an allocation/decompression bootstrap. The full unpacked child payload was not recovered and its internal surveillance behavior is not asserted.

The parent contains remote-thread/DLL attachment and kernel-debug API names, but their diagnostic pointers have no code references in the recovered parent. Preserve those accurate reference observations without claiming executed injection, privilege escalation or screenshots. SHA-1 round code is used for update-file integrity comparison, not evidence of hostile encryption.

Concealed state, remotely supplied executable activation, generated-image logon persistence and own-image cleanup form a covert loader chain. These directly linked effects outweigh ordinary GUI/runtime resources and possible legitimate uses of individual APIs.
missing_context: The original registry package, declared product purpose, operator authorization and deployment history were not supplied. Endpoint responses and the full unpacked child are unavailable. No deployment circumstances were assumed.
changes: Retire the Elex remote-thread conviction: its required evidence was only two Urelas filenames and a neutral API-reference cluster, with no Elex-specific code or bound injection execution. The underlying allocation/write/thread observations remain.

Replace the filename-gated Urelas game-surveillance identity with a complemented-MSMP-code identity plus corroboration. It supplies fallback recognition when the stronger network/storage profiles do not match; it does not claim screenshots. Renaming helper, batch and state artifacts retains hostile recognition.

Relocate the AttachDll diagnostic to DLL-injection references, remote memory API cluster to mem/combined, and GetModuleFileNameA text to current-process information. Matchers, scope and criticality are preserved. Exact consumers follow the new IDs. The fiber ancestor selector explicitly retains the moved memory observation. Its APC consumer uses a logically equivalent fiber-pair exception because APC already requires the allocation/write pair; original exclusions and scope are retained.

Extend the existing Winsock ordinal API-set matcher to preserved original descriptors, checking library/table ownership and a terminated ordinal table including socket/connect/send/recv; ordinary networking remains notable.

Extend the existing Run-write rule to preserved named lookup tables, binding actual IAT operands and HKEY slots. Regression testing preserved both compiler register layouts. Bound instruction fragments avoid the scanner limit of eight matches per YARA pattern.

Add suspicious queried-path retry deletion and notable SCSI WRITE(10) setup. Correct encrypted-resource ZIP recognition to use resource-directory extents instead of assuming a .rsrc section. Unused ZIP bytes under a .rsrc label no longer falsely claim resource membership.

consumers_reviewed.moved_memory: All exact references were updated. The only matching ancestor selector was micro-behaviors/process/create/fiber::fiber-memory-thread-api-profile; its membership is preserved.
consumers_reviewed.moved_module_path: The local self-copy-name composite and HTTP self-upload consumer retain the exact moved observation. No ancestor selectors consumed the old API-resolution directory.
consumers_reviewed.retired_elex_and_old_urelas_identity: No exact consumers. Family fallback keeps MSMP code required and selected artifact names only corroborative.

Carved PE at 0x3e94c has SHA-256 2487929a9293bf783f0330fdee152adf1c6951d65dbf4bf3b98b7b7a860edab8. The old .rsrc pattern matches 16 ZIP headers; the corrected directory-based ZIP trait and WannaCry encrypted-resource identity still fire.

scan_comparison.loss_explanation: Three removed IDs are exact matcher-preserving relocations. The two removed hostile labels overclaimed Elex injection or game surveillance. Supported hostile loader recognition and persistence now fire; no supported attack behavior was deliberately removed.
scan_comparison.disagreement: Raw ML probability rises from 0.8908734 to 0.98023355, while the calibrated fields remain lvl=-1 / class 0. This remains a classifier/calibration miss relative to the MALICIOUS judgment; traits were not duplicated or inaccurately restored to alter it.
scan_comparison.archive_members: The original scan emits only the parent despite the encrypted ZIP resource. The manually recovered child was scanned separately before/after; both retain two suspicious PECompact findings and probability 0.9627836, lvl=-1. No child trait was lost. Automatic embedded-resource traversal remains an engine coverage gap.
